messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈ 0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water is essentially the same as at atmospheric pressure—about **0 °C**.  

The melting curve of water has a very small negative slope (≈ –0.0075 K MPa⁻¹), so a pressure change of only 0.01 MPa (10 kPa) would shift the freezing point by only ~7 × 10⁻⁵ K—well below the resolution of ordinary thermometers. In practice, you can treat the freezing point at 10 kPa as 0 °C.
